title: Walk through a system design question (B2)
summary: Làm rõ yêu cầu, phác thảo thiết kế, nêu một trade-off chính và hỏi lại người phỏng vấn trong khoảng 90 giây.
learningObjectives: Làm rõ yêu cầu và giả định trước khi thiết kế
Trình bày thiết kế theo luồng ghi và đọc
Nêu một trade-off và kiểm tra hướng đi với người phỏng vấn

sections.title: System design prompt
sections.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Interview: Senior Backend Engineer, Tidewater Cloud. Interviewer: Design a service that turns long web addresses into short links. Notes for candidates: ask about scale first, sketch the main parts, explain one trade-off, then check the direction with the interviewer.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Điều hệ thống phải làm hoặc phải đạt trước khi thiết kế.
vocabulary.example: Let me clarify the requirements first.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Nhấn âm tiết thứ hai: re-QUIRE-ment.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Nói rõ điều bạn coi là đúng khi chưa có dữ liệu.
vocabulary.example: I assume ten times more reads than writes.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Nói assume that + mệnh đề, không nói assume about.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Lựa chọn trong đó được cái này thì mất cái kia.
vocabulary.example: The trade-off is between speed and cost.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Dùng giới từ between ... and, không dùng among.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Giữ nhiều bản dữ liệu ở nhiều nơi để chịu lỗi.
vocabulary.example: We replicate the store across two zones.
vocabulary.commonMistake: Động từ có âm cuối /eɪt/, danh từ replica có âm cuối khác.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Thành phần chậm nhất giới hạn cả hệ thống.
vocabulary.example: The database could become a bottleneck.

performanceTask.title: Walk through a design in 90 seconds
performanceTask.scenario: The interviewer asks you to design a service; you clarify, sketch, explain one trade-off and check the direction.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Walk through your design in English in about 90 seconds: clarify requirements, sketch the main parts, explain one trade-off and check the direction. Do not look at the model answer yet.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Speak in English for about 90 seconds: clarify requirements and assumptions, sketch the main parts, explain one trade-off and ask the interviewer if the direction fits.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Let me start by clarifying the requirements. We need to create short links and redirect users quickly, and I assume about one hundred million links with ten times more reads than writes. At a high level, I would use an API service, a key generator and a key-value store. The API receives a long address, asks the generator for a unique code, saves the pair and returns the short link. For reads, a cache sits in front of the store, because most clicks go to a small set of popular links. The main trade-off is between random codes and counters. Random codes are harder to guess, but they can collide, so I would check before saving. Counters avoid collisions, but they need coordination across servers, so I would give each server its own counter range. For reliability, I would replicate the store across two zones and monitor redirect latency. If we had more time, I would discuss analytics and abuse protection. Does this direction match what you had in mind?
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Walk through the design again in English. Keep the four steps and make the trade-off clearer.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Design a different service, such as a notification system, using the same four steps.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Walk through a new design question without looking at old notes.

rubric.label: Requirements, parts, trade-off, check
rubric.description: The walkthrough follows the four steps.

anchors.met: The listener hears requirements, main parts, one trade-off and a direction check in order.
anchors.notMet: Jumps straight to tools or skips the requirement step.

rubric.label: Trade-off reasoning
rubric.description: The trade-off names what is gained and what is lost.

anchors.met: Both options are named with one gain and one cost each.
anchors.notMet: Names one option only or gives no reason.

rubric.label: Checks direction
rubric.description: The candidate invites the interviewer to guide the next step.

anchors.met: Ends with a clear question to the interviewer.
anchors.notMet: Ends with no question or stops abruptly.

audio.text: Before I design anything, let me clarify the expected scale.

pretest.question: What does the speaker do first?
options: Ends the discussion for the team

audio.text: I assume ten times more reads than writes.

pretest.question: What is the speaker doing?
options: Asking for money for the team

audio.text: A cache sits in front of the store, because most clicks go to popular links.

pretest.question: Why is the cache used?
options: Storage is very expensive for the team

audio.text: Does this direction match what you had in mind?
The main trade-off is between random codes and counters.

training.question: What is being compared?
options: Two office layouts for the team
training.feedback: Between ... and nêu hai lựa chọn.

audio.text: Random codes are harder to guess, but they can collide.

training.question: What is the drawback of random codes?
options: They are too long to store
training.feedback: But đánh dấu mặt hạn chế.

audio.text: Counters avoid collisions, but they need coordination across servers.

training.question: What is the cost of counters?
training.feedback: Coordination là cái giá của counters.

audio.text: I would give each server its own counter range.

training.question: What does this approach reduce?
training.feedback: Own range nghĩa là mỗi server tự dùng một dải số.

audio.text: I would replicate the store across two zones for reliability.

training.question: What is the purpose of the copies?
options: Making reads cheaper for the team

audio.text: The database could become a bottleneck at peak traffic.

training.question: What is the concern?
options: A wrong address format for the team
training.feedback: Bottleneck là điểm nghẽn khi tải cao.

audio.text: Let me clarify the requirements, and then I will sketch the design.

posttest.question: What happens first?
options: Drawing the design for the team

audio.text: I assume about a million requests per day.

posttest.question: What is assumed?
options: The server price for the team

audio.text: The trade-off is between latency and consistency.

posttest.question: What is the speaker contrasting?
options: Design and meetings for the team

audio.text: Would you like me to go deeper on storage or on caching?

posttest.question: What is offered?
options: An extra deadline for the team
